rationale.complete: Rounds 1, 1b and 2. Round 2 (2026-10-05) ran the card's R2-R4 with dated predictions and kill rules, synthetic guards on real skeletons (including worlds where talk depends on call length), three amendments before real R3/R4 data, new DQ4 file-level and URL-read tables, 156 estimate rows and period READMEs. Two estimators were rejected by their guards (start-time RD, lag-vs-hop permutation). R1 (reserved-data pre-registration) and R5 (pause-timer cadence) remain.
rationale.faithfulness: The logged light cone holds where it binds (within-room acausal <= 4%; cage in 7/8 two-room periods; NE42 80-860x). Round 2: the ordered-read test of the artifact leak passes pooled (Lambda 1.45 [1.09, 2.26]) but is fragile, and the large read gap is a shared-project field (OR ~290 before and after use in #51). Numbers gate in regime III when pooled with period strata (J_mh,D 3.2), reversing round 1's co-generation reading; but J_mh is post hoc and synthetic worlds show it is biased low by call-length effects.
rationale.usefulness: Operator rule: cross-room leaks go to agents who already work on the source's artifacts (#51: 75% vs 3%), so project membership, not recent fetches, predicts where an item leaks. Fixed rooms cage chat (~100x); hopping rooms leak half the time. Spread runs at ~1 hop per 1.5-5 talk turns; cadence is not a lever.

one_line: Novel items obey a logged read-out light cone in rooms; cross-room leaks follow shared projects, with only a small, fragile ordered-read excess.
